title: Portfolio
text:
A selection of research and academic projects from my BSc in Psychology and MSc in Statistics & Data Science.


The Contexts That Bind Us: Networks, Multiplexity, and Embeddedness in Institutional Domains
Master’s Thesis · Leiden University & CBS (Statistics Netherlands) · 2026
This thesis examines how the organisation of social ties across institutional domains relates to generalised trust in the Netherlands. Using the CBS Person Network, a whole-population multilayer network covering approximately 17 million Dutch residents across five institutional domains (family, household, neighbourhood, workplace, and education), I developed two individual-level dimensions of cross-domain embeddedness. Multiplexity (whether the same people recur across domains) and participation evenness (how evenly a person’s ties are distributed across domains). A key measurement contribution was an adjusted multiplexity measure that accounts for administrative overlap between family and household registers. Person-level measures were linked to the Social Cohesion and Well-being Survey (2020–2023, N = 28,483) to examine their association with generalised trust.
 Thesis



Social Factors Influencing Children’s Pro-Environmental Behaviour
Statistical Consulting Project · Leiden University · 2024
This study investigated how social factors influence pro-environmental behaviour (PEB) in children and adolescents aged 9 to 15 years. Participants (N = 164) from 13 classrooms across two schools completed an effort-based choice task across self, climate, and prosocial targets. We used generalized linear mixed-effects models to examine whether experimentally manipulated social norm messages affect effortful pro-environmental behaviour, and whether individual social susceptibility and classroom cohesion moderated these effects.
 Code



Expanding the Job Demands-Resources Model: The Integrated Work Dynamics Model
Bachelor’s Thesis · Maastricht University · 2024
This literature review introduces the Integrated Work Dynamics (IWD) model, extending the Job Demands-Resources (JD-R) model to better capture the complexities of modern work-life dynamics. Central to the IWD model is the conceptualisation of personality traits as personal demands, offering a new perspective on individual-environment interaction. The review integrates findings from existing literature to identify strategies for tailoring work environments to diverse employee needs, with implications for both theory and practice.
 Thesis


Immigration to Europe: An Interactive Dashboard
EMOS Presentation of Official Statistics · Leiden University · 2025
An interactive Shiny application that visualises immigration patterns across European countries using Eurostat data. The dashboard includes time-series views by country, choropleth maps of immigration counts, and maps showing immigration as a share of the national population. Data were sourced from the Eurostat migration (migr_imm8) and population (demo_pjan) databases, combined with NUTS-0 boundary files for spatial visualisation.
 Live app  Code



Housing Price Statistics in Den Bosch
EMOS Statistical Production Systems · Leiden University · 2025
This project implements a reproducible statistical production pipeline for computing average housing prices in Den Bosch. Using synthetic data from the Dutch buildings register and property sales records, the pipeline follows a five-stage workflow from raw data ingestion through preprocessing, validation, and statistical processing to final output. Each stage is modular and documented, reflecting the production system standards taught in the European Master in Official Statistics (EMOS) programme.

title: CV
text:
My background combines psychology with statistics and data science. I’m interested in using quantitative methods to understand social and behavioural phenomena, including how social contexts shape people’s lives. My methodological interests include psychometrics, structural equation modelling, Bayesian methods, multilevel modelling, and network analysis.



MSc Statistics & Data Science — Leiden University, 2024–2026
Specialisation: European Master in Official Statistics (EMOS)
Thesis: The Contexts That Bind Us: Networks, Multiplexity, and Embeddedness in Institutional Domains (grade 8.0)


BSc Psychology — Maastricht University, 2021–2024
Thesis: Expanding the Job Demands-Resources Model: The Work Dynamics Model (grade 8.5)





Master’s Thesis Intern — Statistics Netherlands (CBS), 2026

Developed measures of institutional embeddedness using nationwide administrative network data covering approximately 17 million residents, examining social connections across family, household, neighbourhood, workplace, and education domains.
Linked population network measures with survey data to investigate how network characteristics, including institutional breadth, participation evenness, and multiplexity, relate to generalised trust.
Processed large-scale register data in R using data.table, arrow, and DuckDB, and conducted statistical analyses using regression models.



Statistical Consulting Project — Leiden University, 2024

Analysed children’s pro-environmental behaviour using clustered classroom data, applying confirmatory factor analysis (CFA), multilevel generalised linear mixed models (GLMMs), and power analysis.
Evaluated methodological considerations related to clustered observations and measurement, using R and Git for reproducible analysis.



Research Practical — Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam, 2023

Investigated the psychometric properties of the Self-Control Scale in workplace settings using reliability analysis, exploratory and confirmatory factor analysis, and multitrait-multimethod (MTMM) correlations.



Research Practical — Maastricht University, 2023

Designed and conducted a between-subjects experiment examining mental health stigma, including study design, power analysis, ethical approval, and participant recruitment.
Analysed experimental data using analysis of variance (ANOVA) and interpreted the findings in relation to the research hypotheses.






Student Assistant — Maastricht University, School of Business and Economics, 2022–2024

Reviewed over 1,000 student applications, advised prospective students, and supported recruitment and information events.



Volunteer Coordinator — Maastricht University, Studium Generale, 2022–2024

Coordinated more than 20 volunteers across three editions of the Pleasure, Art & Science Festival, managing volunteer communications, scheduling, and website support.



Student Ambassador — Maastricht University, Faculty of Psychology and Neuroscience, 2022–2023

Represented the Psychology programme at recruitment events, delivering presentations and answering questions from prospective students.





Statistical modelling: Generalised linear models, multilevel modelling, longitudinal modelling, structural equation modelling, Bayesian methods, and statistical learning.
Measurement and research methodology: Psychometrics, factor analysis, survey methodology, causal inference, missing data methods, and experimental design.
Other quantitative methods: Social network analysis, power analysis, and statistical simulation.
Programming and software: R, Python, Git/GitHub, LaTeX, SPSS, Excel.

title: Milena Costa
text:
Hi! I’m Milena, a quantitative social scientist. I grew up in Brazil and moved to Belgium when I was eighteen, where I worked for two years as an au pair and nanny, while learning Dutch at the KU Leuven. Watching children grow up in a different context than my own made me curious about how the environments we grow up in shape who we become. I have been in the Netherlands for five years now, and am currently based in Leiden.
Through a bachelor’s in Psychology at Maastricht University, I learned to think about behaviour in context. I also discovered a passion for the quantitative side of research, especially the challenge of measuring things that aren’t directly observable, like well-being or social relationships. A master’s in Statistics and Data Science gave me a stronger foundation in statistical modelling, research design, and working with complex data. For my master’s thesis at Statistics Netherlands (CBS), I used a whole-population network of the Netherlands to investigate how people’s embeddedness in different social domains, such as work, neighbourhood, and household, relates to generalised trust. I enjoy applying quantitative methods to answer relevant social questions, finding patterns, and questioning what those patterns actually mean in people’s daily lives.
Going forward, I am looking to continue working in applied statistics, answering questions about how social contexts shape individual outcomes. Methodologically, I am particularly interested in measurement and psychometrics, multilevel and longitudinal modelling, and social network analysis.
Outside of research, you’ll find me taking care of my tropical plants and having deep discussions about the meaning of life. I love learning about new cultures, exploring different perspectives, watching arthouse films, and going down rabbit holes about whatever has caught my attention lately. Whenever I get the chance, I also like to scuba dive.
